title: What moved your money this month
intro: 2026 has been driven by an energy shock and an AI chip boom. India benefits from neither: it imports oil and has little chip exposure. September was a broad risk-off month, and only 16% of Indian sectors went up.

tracker_groups.name: Economy and money
tracker_groups.blurb: Oil, rates and the rupee are where most shocks start. They explain what happened, and to what.

cards.why: India imports over 80% of its oil. Higher oil means higher inflation, a weaker rupee and pressure on margins.
Imports get costlier, but dollar assets gain in rupee terms. A slow grind, not a shock: volatility is about 5%.
The risk-free benchmark. Rising yields hurt long-duration debt funds and make stocks less attractive.
High US rates pull money out of emerging markets, including India.
A strong dollar usually means a weaker rupee and foreign selling.
The base price of money. Moves FD rates, EMIs, bond prices and stock valuations.
Drives RBI decisions. Core shows whether price rises are spreading or temporary.
Negative real rates push money into stocks, gold and property.

world.note: In rupees the Sensex is down about 8%. The rest is the rupee's 6.4% fall, which is our calculation. India's correlation with the US is 0.17, so US equity does genuinely diversify an Indian portfolio.

gap.title: Same funds, very different returns
gap.blurb: Money arrives after the good years and leaves after the bad ones. The fund earns one number; the average rupee in it earns another.

watching.v: Cheap oil is one of India's biggest tailwinds. When it falls, most of the chain runs in reverse.
Three losing years so far. Stability would ease imported inflation and foreign selling.
Up 60 bps this year. A peak would help long-duration debt and equity valuations.
